First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{x+2}{(x-4)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x-4}+\frac{B}{(x-4)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ and $B,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-4)^{2}$ and get

$$
x+2=A(x-4)+B.
$$

Plugging in $x=4,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4+2 & =A(4-4)+B \\ B & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+2 & =A(0-4)+6 \\ 2 & =-4A+6 \\ 4A & =4 \\ A & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{x+2}{(x-4)^{2}}=\frac{1}{x-4}+\frac{6}{(x-4)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{x+2}{(x-4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(\frac{1}{x-4}+\frac{6}{(x-4)^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x+6{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{(x-4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|\,{|}_{1}^{2}-\frac{6}{x-4}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-4|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-4|)-(\frac{6}{2-4}-\frac{6}{1-4}) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)-(-3-(-2)) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3})+1.\end{aligned}
$$
